title: Develop Your 12 Week Plan
hook: Roadmap cards stop being strategy when Lucy has to name the weekly proof on one page.
counterintuition: A plan can feel responsible while still hiding every real choice. The useful move is to convert vision into a few written goals, concrete tactics, and weekly proof that action is actually happening.
tryThisNow: Write one 12 week goal. Under it, add one lead action and the weekly proof that will show the action happened.
keyTakeaway: Convert vision into a written 12 week plan with few goals and concrete tactics that foster execution. The standard is visible action, not a better-sounding intention.

examples.title: Lucy compresses the roadmap

planSpec.audience: a practitioner in health-tech roadmap planning who needs the chapter move under real pressure
planSpec.stakes: the visible result will slip while everyone can still explain the effort
planSpec.requiredBeat: Lucy writes the goal, lead tactic, and weekly proof on one page.

examples.scenario: Roadmap cards cover the product room wall, but Lucy can no longer tell which cards serve the 12 week result. She must decide which goal, lead tactic, and weekly proof fit on one page before the health-tech team adds another feature request to the pile.
examples.whatToDo: Write one goal, the lead tactic that can be acted on this week, and the proof that will be checked every Friday.
examples.whyItMatters: The plan becomes executable when Lucy removes the extra cards. Effective Plan Structure turns the wall into a weekly operating sheet.

examples.title: Olivier cuts the membership list

planSpec.audience: a decision-maker in independent gym membership push choosing whether to protect execution or drift
planSpec.stakes: the next 12 weeks will inherit a soft plan unless the decision is made now
planSpec.requiredBeat: Olivier cuts the membership plan to two goals and four tactics.

examples.scenario: "Are we building memberships or collecting ideas?" Olivier asks while plastic membership tags swing from hooks behind the desk. The gym team must decide before the January push: keep twelve promotion tactics, or cut the plan to two goals and four actions someone can actually complete.
examples.whatToDo: Limit the membership push to the goals and tactics that can survive a normal week of classes, cleaning, and front-desk interruptions.
examples.whyItMatters: Planning is beneficial only when it reduces noise. Olivier protects execution by making the plan smaller and clearer.

examples.title: Anke links boxes to outcome

planSpec.audience: a team lead in legal discovery project who needs visible proof before the week softens
planSpec.stakes: the team will mistake motion for progress if the proof stays hidden
planSpec.requiredBeat: Anke links discovery tasks to the 12 week case outcome.

examples.scenario: You are standing beside evidence boxes and a scanner that has been whining since lunch. Anke must decide whether the discovery plan will count pages processed or serve the 12 week case outcome: the filings ready, the contradictions tagged, and the partner brief clean by the deadline.
examples.whatToDo: Tie each discovery task to the case outcome and delete the tasks that create activity without moving that outcome.
examples.whyItMatters: The team can be busy and still be vague. Anke makes the plan useful by connecting each tactic to the result the case needs.

examples.title: Tomas writes from the table

planSpec.audience: a reflective operator in heritage conservation proposal reading last week's failure as evidence
planSpec.stakes: a repeat failure will be explained away instead of corrected
planSpec.requiredBeat: Tomas turns the proposal vision into a written 12 week plan.

examples.scenario: It took Tomas a rejected draft and three stone samples on the drafting table to see the flaw. The proposal vision was strong, but no one knew what had to be finished by week four. He rewrites the work as a 12 week plan with two goals, dated field visits, and a review point before the council packet is assembled.
examples.whatToDo: Turn the proposal vision into dated tactics and interim proof, not a longer description of why the building matters.
examples.whyItMatters: A conservation proposal needs emotion and structure. Tomas gives the future enough detail to survive procurement dates and council review.

examples.title: Marta changes the tutoring proof

planSpec.audience: a reader in university tutoring center comparing intention before the move with proof after it
planSpec.stakes: the work will stay aspirational unless the action changes in the room
planSpec.requiredBeat: Marta chooses the tutoring center goal and weekly lead measures.

examples.scenario: Tutor schedules run in colored rows across the center window. Before, Marta promised broader student support and tracked appointment totals after the fact. After, she chooses one 12 week goal, assigns weekly outreach blocks, and checks whether first-year math students book help before the exam panic starts.
examples.whatToDo: Pick the tutoring outcome and lead measures before the semester noise arrives. Schedule the weekly actions that create appointments earlier.
examples.whyItMatters: Marta moves from good intention to controllable behavior. The plan respects short-term results without losing the center's long-term capacity.

examples.title: Hiroshi separates capacity from result

planSpec.audience: two colleagues in Madrid export sales team forcing the commitment into plain speech
planSpec.stakes: a public promise will dissolve unless someone names the proof and owner
planSpec.requiredBeat: Hiroshi separates market capacity work from short-term sales result.

examples.scenario: At 3:20 p.m. in the Madrid sales office, Hiroshi sorts export invoices in a mail tray. As team lead, he must decide which work belongs to market capacity and which result must be proved in the next 12 weeks.
examples.whatToDo: Separate capacity work from the short-term sales result, then write both in different places so the team does not pretend one is the other.
examples.whyItMatters: Hiroshi prevents a common planning blur. Long-Term Capacity versus Short-Term Results matters because both are real, but they cannot be measured with the same promise.
